topics.topic: Flow purpose rules on later flow versions for an existing flow (omit/repeat/match/differ handling)
questions: On later compose requests for the same flow, is `purpose` required/allowed, and what happens if it differs from the stored one?
For composing additional versions of an existing flow, what is the rule for `purpose` in the request?
When composing later versions of an existing flow, must purpose be absent, must it match, or is a changed purpose accepted/ignored?

judgement.divergence: One implementer requires a `purpose` on later compose requests and refuses if it differs from the stored flow purpose, while another accepts later compose requests without checking or using any supplied `purpose`; the agent (and owner via inspection outcomes) notices through different accept/refuse results.
judgement.why: The text defines how purpose is set at creation but does not state the rule for later versions of an existing flow.

topics.topic: Slot purpose rules on later contract versions for an existing slot (omit/repeat/match/differ handling)
questions: On later contract-authoring requests for an existing slot, is `purpose` required/allowed, and if provided with a different value is it ignored or refused?
For later contract-version requests on an existing slot, must `purpose` be omitted, repeated identically, or can it differ (and be ignored/refused)?
When issuing later contract versions for an existing slot, must the request omit purpose, repeat the same purpose, or is a differing purpose refused/ignored?

judgement.divergence: One implementer requires later contract-version requests on an existing slot to repeat the same `purpose` and refuses differences, while another ignores any later `purpose` field (or its absence) and proceeds; the agent notices through different authoring success/refusal behaviour.
judgement.why: The text states how slot purpose is established at first creation but leaves later request handling unspecified.

topics.topic: Draft-write authority model: whether attempts rely on flow activation vs per-attempt/standing owner approval, and how that authority is referenced on EffectAttempt
questions: After `not_applied`, must a `draft-write` operation require a per-attempt owner approval (despite normally using flow activation), or does `draft-write` continue to use activation only?
Can a standing grant be created for a `draft-write` node, and if so does it have any authority effect or is it refused as nonsensical?
How is EffectAttempt meant to reference one exact FlowActivation record when multiple activations can exist for the same flow/version over time?

quotes:
At run time each `state-transition`, `external-effect` and
`destructive` node stops for the owner's approval of the exact operation, target
and input, unless the owner granted that exact flow version a standing approval
for that node; `destructive` never takes a grant.

An effect resolved as not applied is sent again only with a fresh
approval, even where a standing approval exists.

`authority`: the approval or the grant it used, or for a `draft-write` send
  the flow activation under which the run started (State 2, A10 rule 6; State
  5) — except a resend after `not_applied`, which, whatever its class, records
  the fresh approval it needed;
judgement.why: These passages already define that draft-write normally uses flow activation, that resend after `not_applied` needs fresh approval, and that grants are only the approval-stopping path with `destructive` excluded.

topics.topic: EffectAttempt status when a run ends while an attempt is still in_flight
questions: If a run is ended (`cancelled`/`refused`/`failed`) while an effect attempt is still `in_flight`, must the attempt be forced to a terminal status (and which one), or may it remain `in_flight` forever?

topics.topic: ManifestOperation semantics when no service instance is selected (existence/readability/base_url)
questions: If no instance is selected for a service, does a ManifestOperation still exist for propose/accept/proof reads, and is `base_url` absent or is manifest reading refused?

topics.topic: Required behavior when a newly minted random identifier collides with an existing record id
questions: What must the kernel do if a newly minted random id collides with an existing record id?

topics.topic: Whether ProofResult is persisted as a historical fact or recomputed transiently over time
questions: Is a proof result at composition/activation time a stored historical fact, or only a transient recomputation that may differ later as external conditions (for example binding acceptance state) change?

topics.topic: Whether State 1 is a frozen normative input or an editable draft that can still change model facts
questions: Should State 1 be treated as normative/frozen input for later states and code generation, or as a changeable draft that can still alter model facts and lifecycles?

topics.topic: Whether TrialExecution references are part of AdmissionVerdict identity or only auxiliary evidence
questions: Are per-admission TrialExecution references (with random ids/timestamps) part of AdmissionVerdict meaning identity, or only attached evidence outside verdict identity?

topics.topic: Whether authoring with an existing slot_id creates a new contract version or is rejected as already taken
questions: When authoring a contract with an existing slot_id, is that valid as a new contract version for that slot, or refused because the name is already taken?
